facts.raw_span: A man in his 50s presented with new and progressive satellite lesions while undergoing pembrolizumab therapy
Two years earlier, he had undergone a wide local excision with graft repair for a left posterior auricular scalp lesion
An incidentally resected lymph node was found to be focally involved, with no evidence of distant metastatic disease
Multiple unresectable satellite lesions appeared
He received 4 cycles of ipilimumab, followed by a second wide local excision when new lesions appeared
Additional satellite lesions developed and he began pembrolizumab therapy, but after 5 cycles, local progression occurred in the satellite lesions
Multiple satellite lesions were present on the left posterior auricular scalp area
clinically regressed lesions with persistent black pigmentation were noted
H&E sections showed intense mixed superficial and deep dermal inflammatory infiltrate composed of numerous neutrophils, histiocytes, eosinophils, and lymphocytes
SOX-10 and MART-1: Highlighted normal melanocytes in basal layer of epidermis only
CD163 and myeloperoxidase: Highlighted histiocytes and neutrophils respectively
complete tumor regression and neutrophil-rich mixed inflammation; MART-1 immunostain confirms complete tumor regression

concepts.why: The patient had a history of melanoma, with an incidentally resected lymph node showing focal involvement and subsequent development of satellite lesions.

The patient developed an intense mixed superficial and deep dermal inflammatory infiltrate composed of numerous neutrophils, histiocytes, eosinophils, and lymphocytes after treatment with pembrolizumab.
The patient experienced local progression of satellite lesions despite treatment with pembrolizumab, indicating resistance to therapy.
The patient developed an inflammatory reaction characterized by an intense mixed superficial and deep dermal inflammatory infiltrate after treatment with pembrolizumab.
The patient developed multiple unresectable satellite lesions after treatment with ipilimumab, which may be related to an immune-related adverse reaction.
The patient had a history of melanoma and developed new satellite lesions, indicating recurrence of the disease.
The patient had normal melanocytes in the basal layer of the epidermis, which is consistent with a dermal melanocytic nevus.
The patient developed an intense mixed superficial and deep dermal inflammatory infiltrate, which is consistent with an inflammatory dermatosis.

rationales.F01: New and progressive satellite lesions while undergoing pembrolizumab therapy suggest treatment-resistant melanoma.
rationales.F03: Incidentally resected lymph node with focal involvement and no distant metastatic disease indicates early-stage melanoma.
rationales.F05: Ipilimumab therapy followed by new lesions suggests immune-related adverse reaction and potential treatment resistance.
rationales.F06: Local progression of satellite lesions after pembrolizumab therapy indicates treatment-resistant melanoma.
rationales.F09: Intense mixed inflammatory infiltrate and neutrophil-rich mixed inflammation suggest immune-related adverse reaction and treatment response.
rationales.F10: Normal melanocytes in basal layer of epidermis only, highlighted by SOX-10 and MART-1, indicate complete tumor regression.
rationales.F12: Complete tumor regression and neutrophil-rich mixed inflammation, confirmed by MART-1 immunostain, suggest effective treatment response.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's history of a previous melanoma lesion, the presence of new and progressive satellite lesions, and the involvement of a lymph node all support the diagnosis of recurrent melanoma.
